Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Overview Each player builds a postal system. To do so, each player tries to build an effective network of post offices in the cities on the board, acquire valuable carriages, and collect bonus tiles. It also helps to get help from the postal officials. When a player acquires a value 7 carriage or has placed all of their houses, the game is in its final round. When the round ends, the game ends immediately. The player with the most victory points wins the game! Playing the game The starting player begins and the others follow in clockwise order. On a player’s turn, they take the following actions in the order shown: 1. The player must draw a city card (either one of the face-up six from the display, or the top card of the city deck). 2. The player must play a city card from their hand to the start or the end of their route, or start a new single-card route. When adding a card to the end of a route, it must be geographically adjacent to the next city in the route. (eg. Carlsruhe may be placed next to Stuttgart, but not Sigmaringen.) A player only has one route at a time: if they are unable to extend their route using the cards in their hand, they must discard it and start a new one! 3. The player may close and score their current route if the route is at least 3 cities in length. When closing a route, a player may place houses in cities along the route: they must either choose a single coloured region and put a house in every city in that region on that route , or put one house in each different region along the route . Upon closing a route, a player must reduce their hand size to 3 by discarding any cards they choose face-up on the discard stack. When a route is closed, its player scores by collecting: a. tiles for the length of their route (for example, a 5 city route scores any remaining 5-length tile) b. tiles for any region (or pair of regions) they now have a house on every city in c. the next carriage, if their route is long enough NOTE: When claiming carriages, players MUST claim them in increasing sizes, first the 3 city carriage, then the fourth etc. Players CAN NOT rush the game by claiming a 7 city carriage and end the game. Carriages can not be skipped. Additionally, the player may call for the support of one official (Postal Carrier, Postmaster, Administrator, or Cartwright) during their turn, performing that official's special ability. Those abilities are: - Postmaster: You draw an extra card. - Postal Carrier: You can add a second card to your route. - Administrator: You clear the six city cards away, replacing them with six new ones. With no cards in hand, you cannot invoke the Administrator. - Cartwright: You may acquire the next highest carriage, even if your route is one or two cities fewer than required (i.e. a 5 city route gets a level 7 carriage). With 3 cities fewer, the Cartwright cannot help. NOTE: When a player starts their turn with zero cards in hand they must call for support from the Postmaster. Then, the next player takes their turn. Game end and scoring The final round is the one in which a player places all of their houses or gets a 7 carriage. Players have an equal number of turns, so play continues until the end of that round. [Rating: 1/10] Just the worst game I've ever played. I did own this one, I played it several times, but It is simply boring and boring and boring. Someone may like it and enjoy it, but that person is not me.

[Rating: 2/10] Uhh...it's better than Ticket to Ride, but that's like saying poop is better than crap as far as I'm concerned.  Seriously folks, most of us have played Ticket To Ride and Web of Power so why is this the "hot" game of the minute?  There is literally NOTHING in this game that either of those games doesn't provide in terms of (_extremely_ limited) decision making, route planning, card drafting, set collecting, and area control. [Rating: 2/10] Abstract and luck driven, Hard to get started-this is a newbie turn-off. Clunky. Dull, frustrating & a LOSER.

[Rating: 2/10] Too luck based (card draw) and very little player interaction.  It's really the combination of the two things that annoy me.  I don't mind a luck based game as long as it's fun.  But the above combination doesn't do it for me.

[Rating: 2/10] I don't see what all of the fuss is about on this one. I played this a number of times, and it just stinks.

[Rating: 2/10] Blech. Andreas Seyfarth follows up Puerto Rico with this? As dry as Madonna. Very close to multi-player solitaire. You can mess with people's plans a little by taking cards you know they need, but it seems to hurt you as much as it hurts them. And the cards get wiped so often that you really are relying on luck to put the cards you need out there. I can't see playing this over the similar Ticket to Ride. At least it's short.

[Rating: 2/10] Not much more than a simple abstract game with a thin theme draped over it and a nice looking board. The biggest problem with the game (there are several) is there's no player interaction what so ever. It's like a four player game of solitaire with the luck of pulling the right card at the right moment having more to do with winning as anything else.  Only for people who like purely abstract games with a high luck factor. In the end there's nothing new or exciting here.

[Rating: 2/10] After two plays.. "It is an excellent light game.  The luck and lack of player interaction may turn some off.  Despite that it is still very engaging to me."  And after 5 plays... Starting to realize there is only really one startegy to win and because of that luck is a larger factor then I first realized.  Still good gateway game."  And after 20 plays... "This has game has become boring luck driven monotony.  Won't use it for gateway anymore either because I can't get excitied to play it."

[Rating: 2/10] What's the point? There's no tension, not much interaction, and any fun to be had is already in much more concentrated form in other games. Life is too short for games like this one.

[Rating: 2/10] TTR reworked as a MPS euro puzzle. Should be fine for those who like Alhambra.   Route building is interesting, but with the scoring and whatnot there's so many things too juggle you won't look at what other players are doing. At all. Just what level of coach they have and that's it. Like BMC, this is a race, but closer to those of euro puzzle engines (it's not an engine, BUT your set collecting is pretty much tied to an excel spread sheet designer made up).
